notes:
Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency agent interactions and high throughput embeddings for fleet telemetry search. Primary ask: predictable reserved GPU capacity + autoscale behavior that won't violate latency SLOs under spiky traffic.

Key requirements (from AE/SE calls):
- 99.9th perc latency SLO: <= 120ms for chat path (p50 target 25-40ms). p99 budget is strict for driving-assist alerts.
- Sustained embedding throughput: 40k vectors/minute during peak batch windows; concurrent short-chat sessions: ~12k qps token-streaming requests.
- Warm-pool requirements: prefer warm pool of models pre-loaded on GPUs (baseline 8x8 A40 equivalent slots) to avoid cold-starts >500ms.
- Scale-up policy: linear + burst headroom; prefer instant vertical scaling via reserved standby GPUs when queue > 1000 requests for >30s.
- Scale-down policy: aggressive scale-down after 5m idle but maintain minimal warm pool to keep median latency stable.
- Queueing behavior: support bounded request queueing with SLA-aware prioritization (safety-critical telemetry higher priority). Backpressure to upstream services; observable queue depth metrics.
- Fallback routing: automatic fallback to quantized model variant if tail latency spikes, with option to route to hosted_api as emergency fallback.
- Reservation planning: initial commit 40 GPUs (4 nodes of 10 gpus) with ability to burst +50% for holiday/field-test windows. Request ROI calc from Redwood Optimize team.
- Networking: VPC peering + dedicated egress paths for EU telemetry; need data residency enforcement for EU customers.

- Cold-starts cause ~300-700ms tail latency for chat when instances need model load.
- Warm instance p99 improved to ~95-110ms for chat path but spikes during embedding batch storms.
- Autoscaler reacted within 60s for large sustained queues but did not fully prevent p99 degradation during simultaneous batch loads.
